title: Complete ESCO v1.2.1 catalogue with Atlas draft learning pathways
source: User-supplied ESCO v1.2.1 JSON-LD classification archive, all released occupations and skill/knowledge concepts; English and Dutch source text, plus existing Atlas-authored learning content and roles.
note: The active ESCO catalogue is reconciled exactly against the archive inventory and its mutually consistent forward/inverse occupation-skill properties. Catalogue coverage is complete for that release; Atlas learning activities and prerequisite links remain incomplete, proposed, and unvalidated. 3 previously represented obsolete concepts are retained for learner-state compatibility. Earlier sample methodology is recorded in historical_sample_note and esco_v025_import.
decomposition: Capability Atlas pilot v0.7: 101 proposed ALUs across software development and testing, tax calculation, electrical testing, foundational numeracy, and supervised basic health observation. Adds a 63-unit expansion across 27 software-developer ESCO skill nodes (13 remaining Essential and 14 selected Optional), with 108 new proposed decomposition and prerequisite relations. Named-language-specific Optional nodes remain grouped as context-dependent technologies rather than duplicated as separate beginner curricula. Capability Atlas expansion v0.19.0 adds two proposed learning units for each of the previously undecomposed unique ESCO Essential skill nodes across the eight occupations. The new strand-specific exercises are source-informed, use fictional cases or controlled simulations, and remain unvalidated; local tax rules, electrical standards and authorization, testing context, and clinical scope govern real practice. Capability Atlas life-role framework v0.20.0 adds three draft roles outside ESCO (Good friend, Parent, Independent adult), with reusable, explicitly Atlas-authored capabilities and two proposed learning activities per capability. Role links distinguish Atlas core and context-dependent capabilities. Social content is informed by LifeComp; parenting content by WHO/UNICEF nurturing-care and parenting guidance; independent-adult content by LifeComp, DigComp, EU/OECD-INFE financial competence, and WHO health literacy. This is a flexible reflective framework, not a validated assessment or a universal prescription. Capability Atlas developmental foundations v0.21.0 adds suggested early communication and numeracy routes: responsive exchanges through first meaningful words/signs/AAC messages, and small quantities through one-to-one counting, cardinality, numeral links, and first addition. These routes connect to caregiver practice and personal-finance learning; they are proposed pathways, not universal developmental schedules or diagnostic criteria. Capability Atlas school-to-qualification bridge v0.22.0 adds partial Atlas mappings to current SLO primary and lower-secondary Dutch and mathematics outcomes, plus the versioned SBB Software developer MBO level 4 qualification dossier (profile 25998, dossier 23399). Official outcomes and qualification requirements are represented as separate nodes; Atlas learning-unit alignments are proposed and partial, not equivalences or claims of qualification readiness. Several official requirements remain unmapped. Capability Atlas v0.24.0 adds three contrasting profession pilots (primary school teacher, cook, motor vehicle mechanic), 15 proposed occupational capabilities, 34 proposed learning activities, four shared communication/numeracy bridge activities, required and optional role links, and proposed paths from existing early communication and first-addition units. Source materials inform topic selection but do not validate the route. The teacher profile explicitly leaves the Dutch Pabo qualification out of scope. Capability Atlas v0.25.0 imports a systematic 40-per-group sample from the official ESCO v1.2.1 Web-service API across the ten ISCO major groups. Each represented ESCO skill receives an optional, generic first-practice placeholder and a proposed recommended bridge from reachable practical-reading foundations; numeric-topic skills also receive a routine-numeracy bridge. These placeholders do not count as required role progress and are not validated learning outcomes. The API sample has not been independently reconciled against a separately downloaded ESCO package. Capability Atlas v0.26.0 adds 5748 two-stage draft breakdowns to previously undecomposed sample skills, with 11496 proposed learning activities. Each new skill breaks into two required progress steps; one recommended edge sequences the context-setting exercise before a bounded application, and recommended links connect the first activity to the existing practical-reading foundation and selected quantitative skills to routine numeracy. Content is label/type-led, Atlas-authored, and unvalidated; military and other hazardous topics use governance or simulation boundaries rather than live operational instruction.
source_note: ESCO occupation-to-skill links retain source identifiers. Learning units, decompositions, prerequisites, classifications, and effort estimates are Atlas-authored proposals; they are not ESCO records or validated prerequisites. The software-development strands are informed by ACM/IEEE curriculum guidance; security concepts are scoped to NIST SSDF practices and the relevant unit-specific boundaries. Life-role capabilities and learning activities are informed by LifeComp, WHO/UNICEF parenting guidance, DigComp, EU/OECD-INFE financial competence, and WHO health literacy; these frameworks inform topic selection but do not validate the Atlas draft. Early-development content draws on ASHA communication milestones and AAC guidance, Harvard serve-and-return resources, and IES early mathematics practice guidance. All links and activities remain Atlas proposals. SLO curriculum outcome records retain their sector, kerndoel code, and status; SBB qualification requirements retain dossier version and source. Partial Atlas alignments do not satisfy or certify official outcomes.

esco_v025_import.sample_method: Systematic selection of up to 40 occupations per ISCO major group, evenly distributed across occupation codes.

esco_v026_breakdown.source_basis: ESCO v1.2.1 skill labels, skill types, and existing ESCO occupation-skill links
esco_v026_breakdown.method: Two stage Atlas draft generated using the ESCO label and knowledge/skill type, with family-specific task framing, assessment criteria, and safe simulation boundaries where indicated.
esco_v026_breakdown.validation: proposed; not independently or occupationally validated

catalogue_scope: All released ESCO v1.2.1 occupations and skill/knowledge concepts from the supplied archive; existing obsolete concepts are retained only for learner-state compatibility.
historical_sample_note: The ESCO occupation and skill concept IDs and Essential/Optional occupation-skill relationships in the broad import are source-backed from the official ESCO Web-service API. The included sample is systematically spread across the ten ISCO major groups, not the complete ESCO occupation catalogue. ESCO links are not prerequisites. Atlas entry-practice units and their recommended bridges to practical reading and selected numeracy are navigation scaffolds only; they are generic, proposed, unvalidated, and do not establish skill mastery, qualification readiness, or authorization to practise. v0.26.0 adds two required Atlas-proposed learning steps to each imported ESCO skill that lacked a detailed breakdown. Activity patterns are tailored by ESCO skill/knowledge type and label families (communication, coordination, inspection, design/documentation, operation, quantitative work, rules/quality, and knowledge). Sensitive or regulated topics are limited to fictional cases, supplied current references, simulation, scope, and escalation boundaries. These draft steps still require occupation-specific practitioner review and do not turn the source ESCO relationships into official learning prerequisites.
